polityNote: Russian Empire (to 1917-11-06). Finnish läänit belong to the Grand Duchy of Finland, in personal union with the Empire from 1809-09-17 (Old Finland/Vyborg gub. joined it 1812); before that the western Finnish läns were Swedish. Courland joined in 1795. German occupation of Courland (1915) and Riga (1917-09) did not change the governorates de jure. Old Style decree dates converted to Gregorian. Scope extended back to Peter I's governorates (29 Dec 1708). Livland is drawn from 1727 (Riga governorate without Smolensk province); Estland only from 1798, because until Paul's re-division the Narva county lands west of the Narova lay in St Petersburg governorate (and before 1775 Narva with its uyezd lay in Reval governorate).

spans.dateNote: Year precision, first year the sources guarantee: the west-bank lands of Narva uyezd outside the town (Joala, today Kreenholm/Joaoru — inside the 1897 Wesenberg uyezd) passed from St Petersburg to Estland in 1797 under Paul's re-division (31 Dec 1796 O.S. = 11 Jan 1797), day not stated. Narva town itself (1897 Yamburg uyezd) was never in Estland in this span (without uyezd 1797–1802, then St Petersburg governorate). Ends with the Provisional Government statute of 30 Mar 1917 O.S. joining northern Livonia to Estland.

sources.title: Лифляндская губерния — Википедия (oldid 155114482)

sources.title: Смоленская губерния — Википедия (oldid 155088315)
sources.says: Smolensk governorate dissolved in 1713, most of it to Riga governorate; re-created in 1726 with five uyezds.

spans.dateNote: Year precision: Smolensk province left Riga governorate when Smolensk governorate was re-created in 1726 (day not found); from 1727 Riga governorate is the five provinces Riga, Wenden, Dorpat, Pernau, Ösel — the later Livland. Riga namestnichestvo 3 Jul 1783 O.S. (nine uyezds), Livland governorate 12 Dec 1796 O.S. No source records a transfer across its lines with Estland (Swedish-era line), Pskov, Polish Inflanty / Vitebsk or Courland (the Düna) between 1727 and 1917. Ends 30 Mar 1917 O.S.
